..
Drier air with precipitable water (PWAT) values around 1.8 inches
continue to sit over the region with drier air aloft, so shower
coverage remains isolated and is expected to continue through the
next several days. Light and variable winds may allow for island-
effect showers before increasing to gentle to moderate out of the
northeast by the end of the work week. Ensemble model guidance 
continues to show a passage anywhere between south of Guam to north 
of Saipan as a tropical storm or typhoon. Uncertainty is still high 
regarding timing, location, and intensity, but the potential for 
heavy rainfall and gusty winds continues to increase as the weekend
approaches. Residents of the Marianas can begin basic early
preparedness tasks such as cleaning storm drains, taking inventory of
storm supplies, and trimming overgrown foliage as well as monitoring
the forecast through the week.

Marine...
Combined seas of 2 to 3 feet are expected for the region as an 
altimetry pass far off to the west indicates 2 to 4 feet. Swells out
of the north and northeast continue to diminish tonight before the
east swell begins to build Wednesday night. Light and variable winds
will shift to the northeast and increase to gentle to moderate by the
end of the work week. Then, the east to northeast swell and winds will
significantly increase over the weekend through early next week.

Hydrology...
Invest 96W is still a broad, disorganized disturbance located about
300 miles north of Kosrae. Ensemble model guidance continues to show
a passage anywhere between south of Guam to north of Saipan as a
tropical storm or typhoon. Uncertainty is still high regarding
timing, location, and intensity, but the potential for locally heavy
rainfall and flooding continues to increase approaching this weekend. 
This is expected to produce 5 to 8 inches of rainfall between 
Saturday and Monday, with localized amounts up to 12 inches possible. 
As showers are likely to persist, consistent rainfall is likely to 
saturate the soils enough to increase chance for mudslides. Residents
on these islands need to closely monitor this developing situation 
as flood watches, advisories, and flash flood warnings could be 
issued later this weekend.

Tropical Systems...
TD 28W continues to head northwest, located at 16.7N 146.4E. 
Recently deep convection has developed along the southern flank, so 
we'll see if this system tries to strengthen or if this is just a 
brief "flare-up". Maximum sustained winds remain at 35 mph. It's 
expected to turn more north than northeast over the next few days, as
it slowly weakens.

The main item of interest has been Invest 96W, located near 9.7N
163.8E, currently located east of Ujelang in the RMI. It was upgraded 
to "Medium" by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center. This means the 
formation of a tropical cyclone is likely, but beyond 24 hours. At
this time, uncertainty has grown as the consistent ECMWF (consistent
the last few days) has trended weaker and further north today,
similar to the GEFS. Meanwhile, the ECAIE, GFS-FV3, GFS-WNV3, and 
the GFS-GENCE remain in lockstep agreement that a potentially 
significant tropical cyclone will pass through the Marianas, much 
stronger than the ECENS and GEFS imply. Given that the system is 
just now starting to show deep convection developing near its LLCC 
(Low-Level Circulation Center), and considering its over 1,300 miles
away from Andersen AFB, "the jury is still out" regarding if it'll 
be a tropical storm/weak typhoon versus something more significant.

The main thing we're telling folks is stay calm, continue to prepare
for a potential tropical storm or typhoon passage, make sure you call
GPA to cut down and limbs near near lines before the storm, stay
informed, and continue to follow us either on social media or at 
weather.gov/gum.

Eastern Micronesia...
The main feature of interest continues to be Invest 96W, which was
upgraded to "Medium" by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center. This means
the formation of a tropical cyclone is likely, but beyond 24 hours.
96W continues to struggle to organize, but the models show this will
change in the next 18 to 48 hours, with the system heading west-
northwest or northwest by Wednesday afternoon, with the inflow into
this tropical disturbance persisting into late Wednesday night or
Thursday. As such, the Special Weather Statement (SPS) was reissued 
for Pohnpei and Kosrae. There, look for locally heavy rainfall and 
isolated wind gusts to 30 knots to remain possible through Thursday. 
Further east at Majuro, you're more removed from the inflow. Still, 
with the Monsoon trough lurking near by, scattered showers remain 
possible the next few days. 

Mariners can expect seas of 5 to 7 feet with gentle to moderate winds
at Pohnpei, Seas of 6 to 9 feet with moderate to strong winds at 
Kosrae, where a Small Craft Advisory remains in effect, and 4 to 6 
feet with light to gentle winds at Majuro. Majuro.
